lines.text: In 1996, one college student actually tried to buy a real fighter jet from Pepsi.
And he had the check to prove it.
See, Pepsi aired a flashy commercial offering prizes for Pepsi Points.
At the end, a teenager flew a Harrier jet to school,
with a joke label reading seven million points.
Drinking seven million sodas was impossible.
Except the fine print let buyers purchase extra points for ten cents each,
Twenty-one-year-old John Leonard did the math.
He raised seven hundred thousand dollars from rich investors,
mailed fifteen bottle points plus a giant check,
and demanded his twenty-three-million-dollar military jet.
Pepsi panicked, mailed the check back, and ended up in federal court.
A judge ruled nobody buys a fighter jet for soda points,
though Pepsi quickly edited the price to seven hundred million.
